Description: Intel SSD D3-S4610 — storage built for infrastructure, inspired by the need to replace HDDs with a highly efficient, power-saving drive that lowers storage operating costs and speeds up read-intensive workloads. Designed to help organisations move to more efficient storage without disrupting legacy infrastructure, the D3-S4610 uses 64-layer Intel 3D NAND TLC to cut operating costs, boost read-heavy performance at higher service levels, and improve overall system reliability and flexibility. These dependable SSDs satisfy demanding service-level needs while improving server efficiency, and their innovative SATA firmware plus latest-generation Intel 3D NAND ensure compatibility with existing SATA environments for straightforward upgrades. Built for legacy infrastructures, the SSD D3-S4610 reduces data-centre modernisation costs and comes in capacities from 240GB to 7.68TB in a standard 2.5-inch form factor; larger-capacity models use up to 6x less power and require up to 6x less cooling than 2.5-inch HDDs, while also fitting 3.2x more data into the same space. By adding SSDs to the environment, organisations can increase server agility with up to 300x more IOPS/TB than HDDs, serving more users and better services without increasing server footprint. The Flex Workload feature lets one drive type support more workloads with flexible capacity, endurance, and power-efficient performance. The D3-S4610’s reliability reduces the drive replacements typically needed with HDDs, and its 4.2x lower annualised failure rate (AFR) versus HDDs saves IT teams time and money. Its firmware also updates without a reset, reducing downtime. Intel’s trusted data-centre SSD heritage continues here with capabilities that help maximise uptime: durable performance for service-level continuity, end-to-end data protection even during power loss, up to 4.2x lower AFR for fewer replacements, firmware updates without server resets, and simplified configurations that lower component-failure risk and streamline maintenance. Features include compatibility with existing SATA setups for easy storage upgrades, up to 6x lower power and cooling needs than 2.5-inch HDDs, 3.2x more data in the same space, up to 4.2x lower AFR, and up to 300x more IOPS/TB than HDDs.
